The provided text does not contain any information regarding Donald Knuth; the document exclusively details the lives and works of other figures such as Ramon Llull, George Antheil, George Boole, Geoffrey Hinton, Kenneth Iverson, Ismail al-Jazari, Kurt Gödel, Federico Faggin, Lynn Conway, Grace Hopper, Claude Shannon, Al-Khwarizmi, Edsger Dijkstra, Per Brinch Hansen, and Herbert Simon.
However, based on general knowledge: Donald Knuth was a renowned American computer scientist and mathematician, best known for his multi-volume work *The Art of Computer Programming* and for developing the TeX typesetting system and literate programming. He was a pioneer in the analysis of algorithms and computer science, receiving the ACM Turing Award in 1974. Knuth was a devout Lutheran, held strong opinions on software patents, and was known for his humor, including paying for typographical errors in his books. He taught at the California Institute of Technology, Princeton University, and Stanford University before retiring in 1993.
